title: A handed-in lane PR cannot fall off the batch runner's list
why: Runner 10 built batches from a list it carried and ran merge --reviewed only for lanes it named, never the --root form whose 'open batch now' line lists every done PR. #2816 and #2848 read done from 03:50 CST Nov 13 and missed batches 124-130 with no reason. #2917 and #2817 read open (fix check passed, no round recorded) and nobody told the lane, which idled waiting on runner 10. #2922 is stacked on #2817. Lane archive-flow's 5 PRs waited from 20:13 CST Nov 12.
source: retrospective 09:19 CST Nov 13; owner 09:16 CST: 'how are we losing track of built work if we have a plan?'
note: Amended 09:27 CST Nov 13 to make it mechanical (owner 09:26 CST: "runner 10 is gonna build that mechanically or it's just known in its handoff? can't we basically have it done better mechanically too?", relayed by the retrospective). (1) merge --batch-build NAME with no PR list takes the done set from merge --reviewed --root itself; leaving out a done PR needs --leave N "reason", and the reason prints in the batch PR body. No carried list. (2) When merge --reviewed reads a handed-in PR's record open or bad, it sends the lane a message through the git mailbox (mail send, address from the PR footer's session), so the lane learns without a runner turn; portable per ruling portable-own-features. (3) Upkeep row in skills/roadmap/build.py: a PR with a review record that no batch took after 6 h. Guard change: test-author red cases first; round 3 net-value test applies.
